model: Honeywell 7800 SERIES burner control (S7800A1142 display) via BASgatewayLX
applies_to: Honeywell 7800 SERIES relay modules (RM/EC7800) with the S7800A1142 keyboard display module providing Modbus, read by a BASgatewayLX.
summary: Gateway profile for the Honeywell 7800 SERIES flame safeguard through the S7800A1142: 283 objects (71 AI, 212 BI), 44 polled by default. It reads the burner control fault code, sequence state and its bit flags (standby, purge, ignition, run, lockout), sequence time, cycles, hours, flame signals, remote-command status bits and timing settings.
notes: Built from Contemporary Controls' BASgatewayLX Modbus device profile Honeywell_7800SERIES_Burner_a_LX.csv; the profile maps the registers in the S7800A1142 Modbus register list (https://www.ccontrols.com/support/dp/65-0288-1-S7800A1142.pdf).
Object instances are the ones this profile assigns when it is loaded into the gateway. A site that edited or rebuilt the profile may use different instances.
Only 44 of the 283 rows are flagged for polling in the profile; the rest are served only after you tick them in the gateway. Their descriptions say "not polled by default".

The CSV has no read/write column: Analog/Binary Inputs are read-only and Analog/Binary Outputs are commandable (priority array), which is how the gateway maps them (access inferred). Descriptions give the Modbus register each object reads.

integration.summary: Read sequence state, run and lockout bits, flame signal and the fault code. The profile has no writable objects; the remote-command bits are read-only here.
setup: The BASgatewayLX presents each Modbus device as its own virtual BACnet device on BACnet IP; give it a unique device instance and Modbus address (serial) or IP address (Modbus TCP) when you add it with this profile.
One BASgatewayLX handles up to 100 Modbus devices and 1000 polled points in total, so leave unneeded rows unpolled.
gotchas: Remote command bits (BI 270-277) are mapped as inputs, so remote off/high fire/low fire/reset cannot be sent through this profile as published.
Unpolled rows do not appear as BACnet objects until enabled in the gateway's device profile page.
